data.title: A review of the impact of formative assessment on student achievement in mathematics
data.venue: NOMAD Nordic Studies in Mathematics Education 22(3)
data.abstract: The results show positive relations between student achievement in mathematics and the ways of doing formative assessment.

summary.claim: Formative assessment approaches are positively related to mathematics achievement (journal articles 2005-2014, Web of Science).
summary.condition: Review of published studies; relations, not causal effects; no pooled effect size in abstract.
summary.gap: Does not address primary-level diagnosis tools or purchasing by tuition centres.

data.text: Singapore tuition centres need faster, evidence-linked diagnosis of primary mathematics learning gaps.
data.basis: Demand. Needs public evidence that (a) diagnosing gaps is valuable for learning and (b) centres spend on it or would pay. Packet v0.1 MKT-01 (SYN hypothesis).
market_queries: tuition centre teachers time spent marking diagnosing students Singapore
formative assessment primary mathematics achievement evidence

data.text: Existing primary mathematics EdTech in Singapore (e.g. KooBits, Geniebook, MOE Student Learning Space) does not offer tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable learning-gap reports sold to tuition centres.
data.basis: Differentiation. Packet v0.1 MKT-02 (UNK). Counter-evidence matters as much as support.

Student Learning Space adaptive learning system mathematics

data.text: The serviceable market is the number of Singapore tuition centres teaching primary mathematics times the annual licence price; the buyer unit is centres, not students.
data.basis: Market size. Student enrolment is context only; a students->centres conversion needs its own source or assumption.

data.reason: Formative assessment is positively related to maths achievement, which supports the value of diagnosis but not that centres would pay for a tool.
